sources.label: ChromeStatus feature 5863985044914176 — Clone into all descendant selectedcontent elements
whatwg/html PR #12263 — Keep all descendant selectedcontent elements up to date (merged spec change)

syntax.rationale: The feature adds no new IDL, element, or attribute: it is a behaviour change to the existing <selectedcontent> element. The page has no dedicated 'syntax' or 'shape of the API' section, so the syntax id sits on the example heading, whose <pre><code> block is the only place the page shows the developer-facing shape — <selectedcontent> markup nested inside <select> and <button>.

inputs.rationale: The inputs are the author-written markup the page's example shows: a <select> containing one or more <button> elements each wrapping a <selectedcontent>, plus the <option> elements whose content is cloned. No new arguments, attributes, or parameters are introduced.

outputs.rationale: The what-this-fixes table states the observable outputs: every <selectedcontent> element in the same <select> is kept in sync when the selection changes (previously only the first in DOM order), and updates during insertion/removal are deferred via post-insertion steps or a microtask.

errors.rationale: The page documents no error or exception path: as a behavioural fix to the existing <selectedcontent> element there is no throwing surface, and no error condition is named anywhere in the page's prose or tables.

context.rationale: The at-a-glance table fixes the exposure context: Shipped in Chrome 150 (Enabled by default), Status Enabled by default, API change 'Behavioural fix — edge cases of the <selectedcontent> element', the spec link whatwg/html#12263, Firefox and Safari 'No signal', and the ChromeStatus record 5863985044914176.

lifecycle.rationale: The only lifecycle-relevant content is the update-timing change in the what-this-fixes table: an update that would occur during DOM insertion or removal steps is deferred via post-insertion steps or a microtask. There is no author-managed construction or teardown.

examples.rationale: The page's single <pre><code> example shows a <select> with two <button> elements each wrapping a <selectedcontent>, and states that after Chrome 150 both are cloned from the selected <option> (before, only the first reflected the selection).

compatibility.rationale: The browser-support table lists Chrome 150+ 'Enabled by default (with this fix)' on all platforms, and Firefox/Safari 'No signal'. The ChromeStatus record corroborates desktop/android/webview 150 and Firefox/Safari 'No signal'.

securityPrivacy.rationale: The change adds no permission, origin, storage, network or script-readable surface; the page's 'security issues' phrase refers to the bug being fixed (updates during DOM insertion) rather than to a new security or privacy contract.

notes: PAGE EDIT (ids only, no prose/structure/styling change): five existing <h2> headings gained ids — at-a-glance (context), what-this-fixes (outputs, errors anchor, lifecycle), syntax on the example heading (syntax, inputs, examples), browser-support (compatibility), see-also (final reference section, no dimension maps to it). Every id sits on the heading element itself, never on a <section>; the page has no <h3> at all, so no heading immediately opens a subheading and no id resolves to an empty fragment. The three canonical ids required by the brief (syntax, browser-support, see-also) are present; at-a-glance and what-this-fixes are the two additional ids the contract needs so that context/outputs/lifecycle map to the fragments that actually contain that content rather than being dodged as not-applicable. SURFACE: a behaviour change to the existing <selectedcontent> element, so the inventory is one item (the element's clone-into-all-descendants / deferred-update behavior) and no second surface is invented. The page's single <pre><code> block is HTML markup, not WebIDL, so the declared-surface check is vacuous here.
